_meta.company: Amazon Development Center U.S., Inc. (AWS Hardware Engineering)
_meta.role: Embedded Software Dev Engineer, AWS Hardware Engineering (PSC)

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering candidate at Rochester Institute of Technology, NY, graduating May 2026, with embedded software and firmware experience in C/C++ on ARM CPUs. Built bare-metal embedded C firmware on STM32 microcontrollers with register-level GPIO, timer, and ADC control plus low-level I2C/SPI/UART drivers, and FreeRTOS-based real-time task coordination with interrupt-driven peripheral handling. Uses Git and GitLab for source control across embedded and software projects, with hands-on testing and validation on physical hardware.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Architected a Mixed Reality headset concept applying software architecture and design patterns to an AI-based real-time chroma keying pipeline without a green screen; produced full claims documentation and BOM.

Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via embedded software development in Python.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Used GitLab for source control management and code review, and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation in a laboratory environment.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 ARM CPU embedded firmware in bare-metal C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a custom low-level I2C driver against GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, and I2C1 registers with no HAL/RTOS abstraction layer.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on an STM32 microcontroller, integrating VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override.
Interfaced an NVIDIA Jetson running YOLOv8 object detection to the STM32 firmware over UART for real-time tracking commands.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Deployed the Jetson-side (ARM CPU) arm bridge as a systemd service (Type=simple, auto-restart with backoff, non-root user/group isolation, environment-file-based config) enabling CI/CD-style continuous deployment and self-recovery without manual intervention, with static IP networking for reliable multi-device communication.
